What can be read is where the three scenarios part furthest against the company's own record, and first-year revenue growth is one such place. The bear rate sits below every fiscal year in the record, including the slowest, fiscal 2024 at {earnings_versus_cash.history.years.1.revenue_growth|pct}. Because Python fades growth in a straight line from this rate to the terminal rate at year ten, a first-year gap this wide carries through the whole forecast. Customer concentration is why the bear case is drawn so low: one customer took {concentration.facts.6.value|pct} of fiscal 2025 revenue and another {concentration.facts.5.value|pct}.

The year-ten operating margin is the second place the scenarios part furthest, and again no grid measures what that does to value. The year-ten margin sets the cash flow the terminal value is built on. How heavily that terminal value weighs depends on the gap between the discount rate and terminal growth, and that gap cannot be read because the discount rate is missing. Terminal growth sits below the risk-free rate of {cost_of_capital.risk_free_rate|pct} in all three cases, the bull closest to it.
